findings.summary: Direct-hit disclosure button does not expose its expanded state.
findings.consequence: Screen-reader users can operate the control and focus moves into the input after opening, but the toggle itself does not announce whether the direct-hit form is expanded or collapsed.
findings.evidence: Line 2606 renders the direct-hit toggle as a plain button with only @click, while lines 2607-2621 reveal a form from gotoHitInputOpen. The surrounding handler toggles/focuses the input, but the template has no aria-expanded or aria-controls relationship for the disclosure state.
findings.recommendation: Add :aria-expanded="gotoHitInputOpen" to the line 2606 button and give the line 2607 form, or a wrapper around it, a stable id referenced by aria-controls.
verification: Inspected owned template lines 2553-2623 for search-hit navigation controls.
Inspected surrounding script handlers toggleGotoHitInput, submitGotoHit, navigateToHit, and hitLookupContext.
Inspected reader behavior tests for direct-hit input; they cover focus/navigation but not disclosure state exposure.

findings.summary: No-hit search navigation exposes enabled commands that cannot act.
findings.consequence: When the backend reports zero hits, users still encounter enabled first-hit, last-hit, and direct-hit controls; each path is rejected by bounds checks without navigation, so assistive technology users get actionable controls for unavailable actions.
findings.evidence: Lines 2572-2607 render hit navigation controls whenever searchState and hitResponse exist, without checking hitResponse.total_hits. The no-hit reader behavior test exercises this reachable state with 0 sökträffar and confirms the controls retain the same URL rather than navigating.
findings.recommendation: Gate the controls on hitResponse.total_hits > 0, or render them disabled with explicit disabled semantics when total_hits is 0.
